sections.html: King County is Washington's most populous county, with Seattle as seat and largest city. Residents numbered 2,269,675 in 2020 and about 2,344,939 in 2025. Cities from Seattle and Bellevue to Kent, Renton, Redmond, Kirkland, Federal Way, Sammamish, Issaquah, Enumclaw, Snoqualmie and North Bend all sit inside the county, plus part of Auburn. Which city and special districts cover your parcel decides the levies on your bill, so two similar houses can carry quite different totals.

sections.h2: Who to call about your King County bill
sections.html:
Three separate county bodies touch your bill. The Department of Assessments sets values, Treasury Operations bills and collects, and the Board of Appeals and Equalization hears valuation disputes. The Board is an independent agency, not a branch of the assessor's office.

OfficeWhat it handlesPhone
Department of AssessmentsValues, parcel records, general questions206-296-7300
Assessments, senior exemptionsSenior and disability relief206-296-3920
King County Tax AdvisorAdvice on property tax matters, including appeals206-477-1060
Board of Appeals and EqualizationValuation appeals206-477-3400
Treasury Operations hotlinePayments, statements, account status206-263-2890
Treasury foreclosure unitParcels in or near tax foreclosure206-263-2649

Treasury is at 201 S. Jackson St., Suite 710, in Seattle's Pioneer Square. The Customer Service Center on the second floor takes in-person payments on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Countywide, 2026 property taxes total $8.4 billion, roughly $770 million or 10% above the $7.7 billion of the year before. Taxable value grew only about 5.4%, from $873 billion to $920 billion, so bills outran values.

Most of the jump traces to measures voters approved, not to rising property values. The county government keeps about 20% of what is collected, spending it on roads, criminal justice and public health. State government, cities, schools and other districts split the rest.

Voters approved these measures for 2026:

  • Seattle: a six-year renewal levy for families, education and preschool, plus a ten-year lid lift for election vouchers.
  • Bothell: a ten-year renewal of the Safe Streets and Sidewalks lid lift.
  • Mercer Island: a $103,160,000 general obligation bond for a new facility.
  • School District 1: replacement capital and education and operations levies.
  • King County: a six-year parks, recreation, trails and open space levy.

Before you price your house, search the parcel in the Assessor's eReal Property tool. It shows valuation, levy rates and sale history.

You owe the first half by April 30 and the second by October 31. When either date lands on a weekend or county holiday, the deadline becomes the next business day. The only mailing is a statement in mid-February. After that you hear nothing unless you request reminders, which the Treasury site offers by text or email.

If April 30 passes unpaid, the entire year becomes delinquent on May 1 and late charges are computed monthly on the full-year amount. You may still pay the first half plus charges before October 31. Miss the second half and monthly charges begin November 1 on that portion. The county points out that state law gives it no power to grant extensions, whatever the reason.

A check by mail or at the counter costs nothing extra. Online, the card fee is 2.35% of the charge with a $2 minimum, and an eCheck is a flat $0.55. If a lender pays from escrow, it usually sends one bulk payment close to the deadline. Contact the lender if your parcel still shows unpaid ten days after the due date.

Think a tax is unlawful or excessive and want to keep the right to sue for a refund? Hand in a separate written statement when you pay, saying you pay under protest and listing every reason.

sections.h2: How to appeal a King County valuation
sections.html:
Once you get a valuation notice, you can contest it with the Board of Appeals and Equalization. Petitions go in through the eAppeals portal, or by mail on forms you download.

The filing window comes from RCW 84.40.038. Whichever falls last controls: July 1 of the assessment year, 30 days after the notice, or a period of up to 60 days where the county legislative authority has set one. Your notice prints the date that applies to you, and the board will clarify at 206-477-3400. Missing it is not always fatal. The board can excuse a late petition for good cause, for instance a family death, serious illness or a documented mail delay.

Appeals turn on market evidence. Collect any of these:

  • Recent sales of comparable homes near yours.
  • A contractor's estimate for defects the assessor has not accounted for.
  • An independent appraisal.
  • Photos and records that expose a wrong lot size, bedroom count or square footage.

Separately, the Assessor takes petitions for a refund when a manifest error in the property description, such as wrong square footage, was used to set value. The look-back can reach six years, depending on the evidence.

The county's reduction program is for owner-occupants aged 61 and over, or retired on disability, with income below the state limit. Apply at TaxRelief.kingcounty.gov or call 206-296-3920. It covers one residence and up to one acre. In a multi-family building, the owner's own unit is the only part that counts. Deferral of taxes is available under certain conditions.

Two other programs matter if you renovate or sell. Adding rooms, a deck or a patio to a single-family home may earn a three-year exemption on the improvement's value, but you must apply before construction is finished. Damaged or destroyed property can qualify for a lower assessed value, and the Assessor's office takes those questions at 206-263-2332.

Sellers normally cover Washington's real estate excise tax, and the amount tracks the sale price. The county treasurer is owed the money as of the day of sale, even if recording happens later. A month of delay brings penalties and interest. Should the seller fail to pay, responsibility shifts to the buyer and the tax can attach to the property as a lien.

Washington's state share climbs in steps. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 are taxed by the Department of Revenue at 1.1% on the first $551,000, 1.28% up to $1,551,000, 2.75% up to $3,051,000, and 3% beyond. Your city's local rate is extra. Treasury or your closing agent can quote the total.

Read the tax statement for non-tax charges too. These vary by location and include surface water management, City of Seattle drainage, fire protection, King Conservation District and noxious weed fees. If a new house or addition was never assessed, an omit tax can reach back up to three years and is billed with an extra year to pay.

sections.h2: Can you sell a King County house that is behind on taxes?
sections.html:
Yes. Late charges on a delinquent parcel grow each month, though, so request a current payoff figure from Treasury before you fix a closing date. Call the hotline at 206-263-2890. For any parcel in foreclosure use 206-263-2649, because foreclosure costs are added and cannot be paid online.

Payment plans exist for past due prior-year taxes. A plan lasts no more than 12 months, late charges are not reduced, each plan carries a one-time $100 setup fee, and a vendor adds a monthly processing fee. Taxes three years or more past due can go to foreclosure. An owner who lives in the home and has limited income can request a waiver of interest and penalties as that three-year mark nears, as RCW 84.56.020 describes.

If time is the problem, a direct sale to a cash buyer may close before the tax situation worsens. Weigh it against a regular listing and against a payment plan.

faqs.q: When are King County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due April 30 and the second October 31. A weekend date, like October 31 in 2026, moves to the next business day. After that, unpaid tax collects monthly late charges.

faqs.q: Where do I file a King County valuation appeal?
faqs.a: With the Board of Appeals and Equalization, online through eAppeals or by mail. It is separate from the Assessor and answers at 206-477-3400.

faqs.q: Who pays real estate excise tax when I sell in King County?
faqs.a: The seller, in most sales. It is owed to the county treasurer when the sale occurs. Price sets the state rate, a local rate is added, and Treasury or your closing agent can give the total.

faqs.q: Can seniors lower their King County property tax?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Occupant-owners who are 61 or older, or retired due to disability, may qualify with income under the state limit. Apply at TaxRelief.kingcounty.gov or call 206-296-3920.

faqs.q: Does King County offer a payment plan for back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, for prior-year taxes that are past due. Plans run up to 12 months, late charges still apply, and there is a one-time $100 setup fee per plan. Call 206-263-2649 or email PaymentPlans@kingcounty.gov.
